DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 127 s. 2022 October 11, 2022 MR. NORBERTO PEJI Ppeji0297@gmaiI.com Dear Mr. Peji: This refers to your electronic mail dated 6 September 2022 concerning the declaration of a local non-working holiday in the Municipality of Mendez, Province of Cavite. Per the attached endorsement letter dated 5 September 2022 from the Executive Assistant of the aforesaid municipality was issued to "formally" refer Municipal Resolution No. 75-2000 or the Resolution Adopting Municipal Ordinance No. 80-2000 Declaring September 6 of every year as a Special Non-working Holiday within the Municipality. Hence, the subject query: Whether the local qovernment unit has the power to declare a local non-working holiday. In reply thereto, please be informed that the authority to declare local holidays—be it working or non-working—is vested with the Congress of the Philippines or the President (pursuant to Section 27 of Executive Order No. 292 or the Administrative Code of 1987). The only ramification if the local special day is declared by the President is that it lacks permanence, thus, the declaration need to be made yearly. On the other hand, if the local holiday is declared by the Congress, it is permanent. Nowhere in the Local Government Code of 1991 (Republic Act No. 7160) or any other laws for that matter, can we find a provision that expressly grant the local government the power to declare holidays. Verily, local government units are not clothed with the power to declare local holidays in their respective jurisdiction. This has been our stand as early as in DILG Legal Opinion No. 66, 2000, thus: "xxx please be informed that Executive Order No. 292, othetwise known as the Administrative Code of 1987, expressly provides that 'The President may proclaim any local special day for a particular date, group or place' (Sec, 27, Chapter 7, Introductory Provisions, Supra). Accordingly, since the afore-cited provision negates any authority of the local chief executive concerned to declare a non-working holiday, the alleged Office Memorandum No. 7, s. 2000, declaring 19 April 2000 as a non-working holiday, is null and void, the same being within the authority of the President to do so." Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Therefore, the declaration of a non-working holiday in a particular municipality appears to be without basis. Notwithstanding, it is to be remarked that this Department is an agency under the executive branch of the government and as such, it has no authority to declare invalid any ordinance or resolution duly approved by the local sanggunians, or any act committed by the members thereof which alleged to be in violation of RA 7160 or other applicable laws. Only the courts have the authority to do so upon initiation of the appropriate action. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, By the Authority of the Secretary: ATTY. OR R. LLAMAS for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs Unde re OU E JVULLLS-LRALLD,tam.'clp Dir. ARIEL O.
